summary: Complete artifact package for the manuscript "Distilling Frozen Time-Series Foundation Model Teachers into Lightweight Edge Anomaly Detectors: A Preregistered Quality–Fidelity–Cost Study" (submitted to The Journal of Supercomputing). Contains: (1) all pipeline code (teacher scoring, student training, five-arm distillation, export/timing, statistics, figures); (2) the preregistration v1.0 with the full R1–R17 append-only SHA-256 hash chain; (3) per-run JSON results of the 1,856-run study (400 main grid + 420 auxiliary + 450 five-arm confirmation + 586 disclosed controls and additions), including the second-teacher (TimesFM), third-teacher (Moirai), shuffled-teacher, interface-ablation, anomaly-exposure, capacity-sweep, classical-baseline, and tenth-source extension controls; (4) 36 trained ONNX/INT8 student artifacts with the deployment timing matrix (Raspberry Pi 4B and desktop, single-thread). Benchmark data are public; teacher score caches are regenerable via the included scripts.
title: Artifact package for: Distilling Frozen Time-Series Foundation Model Teachers into Lightweight Edge Anomaly Detectors — A Preregistered Quality–Fidelity–Cost Study

Particle-size tails, manufactured and biofluid-transformed surface identity, true payload localization, release kinetics, residues and analytical visibility must be measured on representative units from the same unselected batch and adjudicated with their covariance intact. The volume treats the manufacturing process and the measurement system as two coupled sources of risk. Microfluidic mixing time, nucleation, residence-time distribution, fouling, raw-material variation and tenfold scale-up are challenged alongside detector saturation, weighting conversion, dilution artifacts, separation recovery and convenience sampling. A process is not accepted when the analytical chain cannot see the defect it is expected to exclude. The monograph contains 30 distinct mathematical research plates, 82 chapters, 410 independently paginated section studies, 200 detailed Research Gates and 33 genuinely distinguishable Phoenix Answer Embryos. Every Gate begins with a large deep-navy bold question and continues with a blind protocol, evidence package, competing explanation, hard stop and successor fork. The central evidence object is the Carrier Quality Provenance Matrix. It binds raw-material identity, mixer geometry, delivered flows, collection time, sampling inclusion probabilities, raw analytical signals, size and interface distributions, payload mass closure, release curves, storage history and release vetoes. It preserves failed runs and abstentions rather than allowing successful aliquots to redefine the lot.

summary: This conceptual theory-building paper develops an interdisciplinary framework for understanding cancer as a model-admissible, potentially persistent system state emerging within complex adaptive biological systems. Building upon evolutionary oncology, dynamical systems theory, cancer-attractor research, tumor plasticity, and adaptive therapy, the study examines how malignant cellular populations may achieve conditional persistence through feedback, selection, environmental constraints, and adaptive reorganization. The central proposition distinguishes biological possibility, dynamical stability, and clinical desirability. Cancer is not described as beneficial or universally stable, but as a pathological configuration whose emergence and persistence may be investigated through formal systems models. The paper integrates three author-developed research architectures: the Akarkach Seven-Stage Emergence Model (A7SEM), A7SEM Reverse, and Pre-Inference Governance Architecture (PIGA). A7SEM provides seven interacting analytical dimensions for studying emergent configurations across biological systems. A7SEM Reverse examines counterhypotheses, contradictory evidence, dependency structures, and falsifiability. PIGA separates the admission of scientific inferences from authorization for consequential actions. Four testable research hypotheses, competing explanations, mathematical templates, and falsification criteria are presented. The framework is further connected to artificial intelligence through structural comparisons involving emergence, uncertainty, observability, and system governance. The study extends the theoretical foundations of the monograph Cancer as a Legitimate System State and connects related publications within the Faith Poetry Research Series. Its principal contribution is an integrated evolutionary, systems-theoretical, and epistemic framework for investigating malignant persistence without conflating mathematical coherence with empirical confirmation or clinical validity. This publication presents theoretical research and a proposed empirical research agenda. It does not establish a validated clinical prediction model, diagnostic procedure, or cancer treatment.

summary: Here I show my solution to the Hodge Conjecture using my framework and ansatz formulation. The paper starts in 1D, from a simple sieve in mod 9 to a continuum projection, then from a 2D variety in mod 9k, to a continuum projection in 2D which can be map to any elliptic curve with Hasse-Weil operator, doing it back and forward with the inverse operator, linking elliptic curves with continuum topologies or fluid fields, and discovering that the Hasse-Weil function can be the filter we need to detect anomalies, this can allow us to extend this framework to higher dimensions with the master ansatz in 3D.
title: Discrete-Continuum Topology and the Hodge Conjecture: A Compressible Maxwell-Navier-Stokes and Modulo-9 Sieve Framework

The paper starts in 1D, from a simple sieve in mod 9 to a continuum projection, then from a 2D variety in mod 9k, to a continuum projection in 2D which can be map to any elliptic curve with Hasse-Weil operator, doing it back and forward with the inverse operator, linking elliptic curves with continuum topologies or fluid fields, and discovering that the Hasse-Weil function can be the filter we need to detect anomalies, this can allow us to extend this framework to higher dimensions with the master ansatz in 3D.

summary: Highlights of the Study This comprehensive review examines the fatigue behaviour of load-bearing polymeric bone scaffolds , addressing a critical but comparatively underexplored aspect of bone tissue engineering. It evaluates the mechanisms governing fatigue damage and systematically examines how polymer characteristics, microstructure, reinforcing materials, scaffold topology, manufacturing methods, loading conditions, body fluids, and tissue ingrowth influence fatigue performance, with particular emphasis on translating polymeric scaffolds toward reliable load-bearing clinical applications. Key findings: 🟢 Fatigue failure mechanisms: Polymeric scaffolds can undergo both mechanical and thermal fatigue. Repeated cyclic loading causes residual-strain accumulation, stiffness and peak-stress reduction, crack development, and hysteretic heating, which can progressively degrade polymer chains and ultimately cause structural failure. 🟢 Low- and high-cycle fatigue: Low-cycle fatigue generally occurs under relatively high stresses and involves repeated plastic deformation, whereas high-cycle fatigue develops over much larger numbers of cycles under lower stress levels and is primarily associated with elastic deformation and progressive material degradation. 🟢 Material and microstructural effects: Polymer fatigue resistance is strongly governed by molecular and microstructural characteristics. Increased crystallinity, molecular weight, and molecular-chain entanglement can improve fatigue resistance, emphasizing the importance of selecting and tailoring the polymer microstructure for load-bearing scaffolds. 🟢 Reinforcement strategy: Incorporating ceramic or metallic reinforcing phases can substantially improve the fatigue performance of polymeric scaffolds by redistributing applied loads and dissipating energy that would otherwise contribute to polymer deformation and heat generation. 🟢 Hydroxyapatite reinforcement: Incorporation of 15 wt% hydroxyapatite increased the fatigue limit of PLA scaffolds by approximately 17%, while also improving compressive modulus, crack resistance, and hysteresis energy compared with unreinforced PLA. 🟢 Scaffold topology: Pore architecture plays a decisive role in fatigue behaviour by controlling stress distribution and stress concentration. Even scaffolds fabricated from the same polymer and having comparable porosity can exhibit substantially different fatigue lives when their pore geometry and filament arrangement are changed. 🟢 Topology-dependent fatigue life: Among 3D-printed PLA scaffolds with comparable porosity, the tetragonal topology achieved a fatigue life of approximately 4400 cycles, outperforming hexagonal and wheel-like structures at approximately 3200 and 2500 cycles, respectively. 🟢 Advanced scaffold architectures: TPMS, Voronoi, functionally graded, auxetic, and other irregular architectures offer promising approaches for load-bearing scaffolds. TPMS structures are particularly attractive because their smooth transitions at strut junctions may reduce stress concentrations, although their polymer fatigue behaviour remains insufficiently investigated. 🟢 Bone-inspired architecture: Bio-inspired scaffold design can substantially improve fatigue performance. Increasing the thickness of transverse rod-like struts in bone-inspired structures was reported to enhance fatigue life by approximately 10–100 times with relatively minor effects on density and stiffness. 🟢 Porosity–strength trade-off: Increasing porosity promotes permeability, vascularization, cell migration, and tissue ingrowth but simultaneously reduces scaffold stiffness, strength, and load-bearing capacity. Therefore, successful scaffold design requires balancing biological benefits against fatigue and mechanical integrity. 🟢 Stress concentration: Geometrical discontinuities and sharp pore corners create localized stress concentrations that accelerate fatigue damage. summary: Setting up each iteration of a parallel Loop took about 6 seconds on a job directory where writes to disk are slow (ChemAI's /D3), so a 161-iteration loop spent 16 minutes before starting any calculation. The iteration's copy of the database was written in about 70 separate commits; it is now one, taking 0.1-0.2 seconds. The baseline copy each iteration is compared against when its results are merged is now forced to disk before the iteration is used, so that a crash or reboot cannot leave a damaged baseline that a restarted job would trust.

summary: This repository contains the primary data files, analytical matrices, and reproducible R scripts supporting the investigation into eco-morphological decoupling and trophic generalism among sympatric cichlid species in the Cross River Basin, Nigeria. Fully documented R scripts used for data validation, matrix-level association testing, and figure generation. These resources provide complete transparency and enable the direct replication of all statistical analyses and permutation tests.

summary: This repository provides the replication package for the manuscript Household Vulnerability Screening under Temporal Drift: Evaluation Design, Calibration and Coverage . It contains the code, documentation, generated figures, generated tables, software requirements, and workflow automation scripts designed to support reproduction of the reported analyses. The package is centred on a Python-based analytical workflow covering data preparation, quality checks, variable construction, operationalisation of the Stress × Savings framework, four-state household vulnerability classification, predictive modelling, probability calibration, validation, robustness analyses, and out-of-time performance assessment. A detailed replication guide documents the computational environment, execution sequence, expected inputs, and procedures used to reproduce the reported results. A separate base-R script is provided as an independent cross-check of selected statistical outputs. The underlying survey microdata are not redistributed in this repository. Researchers must obtain the data separately from the World Bank Microdata Library's  Listening to the Citizens of Uzbekistan Survey 2018–2025 (study identifier UZB_2018-2025_L2CU_v03_M), subject to the provider's access conditions. The study is available at: https://microdata.worldbank.org/catalog/6412.
title: Replication Package for "Household Vulnerability Screening Under Temporal Drift"

summary: Related: Verification Theater: Measured Failure Modes of AI Verifier Panels , accepted (poster) at the NeurIPS 2026 workshop Who Verifies the Agents? Version of record: SSRN 7653679 , DOI 10.2139/ssrn.7653679 . Cite that version. The same text is also at polyhelper.ai/research/sealed-before-the-open/ and https://github.com/vadimchernets/papers/tree/main/sealed-before-the-open . The registered predictions of Section 8 are on OSF: 10.17605/OSF.IO/9Q86N . The immutable release of the open league files on which every number of the paper rests: 10.5281/zenodo.23552700 . The live league and its open data (CC BY 4.0): trends.polyhelper.ai/markets , trends.polyhelper.ai/api/v1 . This deposit is an archival copy made so that the full text stays retrievable; it makes no separate claim. When an AI model says gold will rise, anyone can score the call at the close, but few can check when it was made. A backtest mixes memory with skill, and an operator's log asks for trust. I propose a standard for measuring AI market forecasts, written as a ladder of checkable requirements, and I run its reference implementation, AI Council · Markets: an open league where fourteen models, seven from US and seven from Chinese laboratories, face one question on one price snapshot. Before each New York open the ten on its Council, five from each side, give probabilities for twelve indicators at four horizons. Each answer is sealed into a hash chain before the price it is scored from, the chain is anchored in Bitcoin and signed by independent time-stamping authorities, and one run per session counts by a rule declared in advance. On 21 October 2026, the first counted morning, every counted answer was signed before the 09:30 ET open. Agreement among the models proved to be a count of independent voices, not a headcount: on two development mornings the seven and eight models sealed before the open were as alike as about 1.6 independent forecasters, nine counted ones were worth 2.23, and the closest pairs crossed the US-China line. Check a seal with three commands, and score my thirty predictions, registered on OSF, before I do.
title: Sealed Before the Open: A Verifiable Standard for Measuring AI Forecasts of Financial Markets

Before each New York open the ten on its Council, five from each side, give probabilities for twelve indicators at four horizons. Each answer is sealed into a hash chain before the price it is scored from, the chain is anchored in Bitcoin and signed by independent time-stamping authorities, and one run per session counts by a rule declared in advance. On 21 October 2026, the first counted morning, every counted answer was signed before the 09:30 ET open. Agreement among the models proved to be a count of independent voices, not a headcount: on two development mornings the seven and eight models sealed before the open were as alike as about 1.6 independent forecasters, nine counted ones were worth 2.23, and the closest pairs crossed the US-China line. Check a seal with three commands, and score my thirty predictions, registered on OSF, before I do.

summary: Full FHOPS 1.0.1 rolling-horizon re-run outputs, with the M7 cold-MIP re-run replacing the MIP arm. What changed since v1.1.0-rerun M7 cold-MIP re-run ( 9f0ab69 ): the 117 MIP runs were re-run with the simulated-annealing phase idle (1,800 s stage 1, 900 s earliness, one Gurobi thread per window, 36 windows in parallel), together with the size-40 7,200 s baseline sensitivity runs and the resumed SA run for ni_40_sub112_lock1 . The re-run did not confirm the contention hypothesis. Matching 603,700 per-solve Gurobi records, its work rate was 8.4% higher (median 0.523 → 0.567 work units/s), yet it produced more failures: no-solution windows 9 → 32, empty windows 18 → 39. 20 of 117 runs changed; the long lock1 trajectories diverge, the short ones are identical. The counts describe a time-limited solve, not a fixed property of each instance. Contents data/output/rerun_v101_gurobi/ — SA arm (117 runs) and the original MIP arm. data/output/rerun_v101_gurobi_alone/ — the M7 cold-MIP re-run (117 runs). data/output/rerun_v101_gurobi_sensitivity_* — 7,200 s baseline sensitivity runs. Per-run JSON summaries, stitched assignment tables, solver logs, summary.csv , and the runner / probe / calibration scripts. The paper built from this deposit is UBC-FRESH/fhops-cjfr-rolling-horizon ; its analysis script replays every stitched plan against the full scenario.

summary: Spatial Methods Workbench is a citation-aware R Shiny environment with 12 guided workflows for spatial autocorrelation, conditional networks, spatially adjusted 2D and 3D networks, spatially varying networks, prediction, clustering, image-regression screening, mediation, and statistical shape analysis. Version 0.4.0 re-targets the three advanced network paths to the current public engines. The ISPat 2D and ISPat 3D paths call the CRAN package ISPAT3D 0.3.1 ( ispat3d_fit_2d for the section-wise planar fit and ispat3d_fit for the pooled volumetric fit: Matern-3/2 Vecchia Gaussian-process adjustment on spatially balanced anchors followed by a shared-plus-zone factor covariance fitted by Gaussian maximum likelihood, reported as signed zone partial correlations). The GP-GHS path calls GPGHS 1.0.1 ( gpghs_graph ) with the shrinkage-factor selection rule and AND symmetry of the accompanying article, and returns the GPGHS edge table with scores and signs. The retired ISPAT 0.1.0, ISPAT3D 0.1.1, and GPGHS 0.1.0 interfaces targeted by v0.3.1 no longer exist upstream. New controls expose factor rank, anchor budget, Vecchia neighbors, optimizer iterations, section handling, threads, and seeds; readiness checks require at least two zones with more rows than markers; result manifests record the engine package, version, and function; and real adapter smoke tests run whenever the engines are installed. This complete source distribution contains the installable Workbench package, Shiny application, five executable vignettes, compact simulated datasets, complete documentation, automated checks, and locally bundled package sources for the exact CRAN ISPAT3D 0.3.1 and GPGHS 1.0.1 engines. install-complete.R installs those local engine copies and the single compiled dependency gpboost without cloning their repositories. A curated public-source bundle also preserves license-safe regression, clustering, neural, SV-NN, STCAR, and SBLF source connected to the Workbench adaptations and related-method provenance. Exact engine calls, built-in adaptations, and related screening workflows remain explicitly distinguished. Large curriculum translations, media, Git history, and platform-specific compiled objects are omitted because they do not execute a Workbench analysis. Installation Download and extract the release, then run Rscript install-complete.R , Rscript verify-installation.R , and Rscript tests/testthat.R . The README contains platform prerequisites, engine options, verification, local launch, Docker, privacy, and troubleshooting guidance. Missing CRAN dependencies may be downloaded; the two direct method repositories do not need to be downloaded separately. Required attribution Users must cite this software release and the method-specific publications or software applicable to the workflow used. The complete bibliography is included in REFERENCES.md and in result bundles. Public sources are identified by repository, commit, version, license, retained scope, and role in vendor/manifest.json . Funding acknowledgement Research reported in this software was supported by the National Cancer Institute of the National Institutes of Health under Award Number R37CA214955-01A1. The content is solely the responsibility of the author and does not necessarily represent the official views of the National Institutes of Health. Only public, release-scoped material is included in this record.

summary: TripLibre is an open-source, local-first iOS application designed for personal mobility tracking and travel behavior research. It records location data in the background, reconstructs daily travel activities into visits, trips, transportation modes, and trip chains. It allows users to review and correct inferred travel records. The application supports exporting structured mobility datasets in CSV, JSON, GeoJSON, and SQLite formats, with a Python loader for further analysis. By combining automated GPS-based travel detection with user-controlled data management, TripLibre aims to lower the technical and financial barriers to collecting travel behavior data. Its broader vision is to provide researchers, educational institutions, and resource-constrained communities with an accessible and adaptable alternative to proprietary travel survey technologies, while preserving individual control over sensitive location information. Documentation: https://hhtdiary.org/triplibre/docs/

summary: TripLibre is an open-source, local-first iOS application designed for personal mobility tracking and travel behavior research. It records location data in the background, reconstructs daily travel activities into visits, trips, transportation modes, and trip chains. It allows users to review and correct inferred travel records. The application supports exporting structured mobility datasets in CSV, JSON, GeoJSON, and SQLite formats, with a Python loader for further analysis. By combining automated GPS-based travel detection with user-controlled data management, TripLibre aims to lower the technical and financial barriers to collecting travel behavior data. Its broader vision is to provide researchers, educational institutions, and resource-constrained communities with an accessible and adaptable alternative to proprietary travel survey technologies, while preserving individual control over sensitive location information. summary: RASHER begins as a fork of BACoN 0.4.0 (commit 4fdec16, which includes the samtools consensus -C 20 change below), adapted to Illumina short reads. Everything under "BACoN changelog" is the parent tool's history, kept for provenance. Changed Renamed throughout: the package, command, log ( rasher.log ) and lock file ( .rasher.lock ) are rasher . The pipeline reads Illumina short reads , paired or single-end. sample_R1 / sample_R2 , sample_1 / _2 sample.R1 / .R2 and sample.1 / .2 files (bcl2fastq _001 tails included) pair into one sample, in flat folders, subfolders and sample sheets; a file without a mate is a single-end sample, and unmated files next to a sample's pairs are skipped with a warning. A pair is baited whole when either mate matches the reference, mates travel together through every step ( 1_extracted/<sample>_R1/_R2 , 2_filtered/... ), and a desynchronised pair is an error, whether the mates carry identical names or /1 /2 suffixes. Baiting aligns with minimap2 -x sr (BBDuk baits pairs natively with in2= / outm2= ). --keep-bam now keeps the baited reads aligned to the reference (paired samples: a proper paired BAM). Filtering: fastp (adapter trimming, quality and length filters; its JSON and HTML reports land in logs/2_filter/ where MultiQC finds them) followed by deterministic, evenly spread subsampling of the reads (pairs kept whole) to --target-depth . Filtlong, --keep-percent and --filter-by-reference are gone; --min-read-length defaults to 50. Fasta reads skip fastp and are filtered by length. Templated assembly aligns pairs with minimap2 -ax sr and calls samtools consensus -X hiseq (call quality at least 20, as BACoN's unreleased change at the time of the fork). De novo assembly: SKESA ( -a skesa ; the recommended de novo assembler — on the real-data benchmark its SNP distances matched SPAdes' with far fewer contigs) or SPAdes ( -a spades , --isolate ; writes the assembly graph, more robust below ~30x depth). Flye and myloasm are gone, with --read-type and --min-size . --snp-method auto is minimap2 for templated assemblies and SKA2 for SPAdes and SKESA assemblies. -m/--memory also sizes SPAdes and SKESA (it was BBDuk-only). A paired sample X next to a sample named X_R1 or X_R2 is an error (their outputs would collide). No assembler flags circular contigs any more, so SKA2's circular-contig end extension no longer applies. Single-end extraction matches read names with a trailing /1 or /2 stripped, as aligners report them. Output folders of BACoN do not resume under RASHER (the checkpoint fingerprints are seeded with the tool's name; every step runs again); BACoN VCFs are rewritten. Checkpoints record each step's own output signature, and a result is only reused when its output is still the file it wrote: a sample returning to a sheet can no longer pick up reads another sample wrote over. Switching a sample between single-end and paired (or fasta and fastq) removes the other shape's files. BBDuk's paired outputs are checked mate against mate, like minimap2's (a desynchronised pair fails the sample); mates named .1 / .2 ( fastq-dump --readids ) pair; the unpaired-reads file of fasterq-dump --split-3 next to its pair is skipped with a warning; a file cannot pair with a link to itself, and files that look like mates but do not pair are warned about. Stale fastp reports are removed on rerun and for samples that fail at baiting. The report and MultiQC drop the circular-contigs column (no short-read assembler flags circles) and say that read pairs were kept whole when either mate matched.
title: RASHER: Bait, Assemble and Compare Illumina short reads

The pipeline reads Illumina short reads , paired or single-end. sample_R1 / sample_R2 , sample_1 / _2 sample.R1 / .R2 and sample.1 / .2 files (bcl2fastq _001 tails included) pair into one sample, in flat folders, subfolders and sample sheets; a file without a mate is a single-end sample, and unmated files next to a sample's pairs are skipped with a warning. A pair is baited whole when either mate matches the reference, mates travel together through every step ( 1_extracted/<sample>_R1/_R2 , 2_filtered/... ), and a desynchronised pair is an error, whether the mates carry identical names or /1 /2 suffixes. Baiting aligns with minimap2 -x sr (BBDuk baits pairs natively with in2= / outm2= ). --keep-bam now keeps the baited reads aligned to the reference (paired samples: a proper paired BAM). Filtering: fastp (adapter trimming, quality and length filters; its JSON and HTML reports land in logs/2_filter/ where MultiQC finds them) followed by deterministic, evenly spread subsampling of the reads (pairs kept whole) to --target-depth . Filtlong, --keep-percent and --filter-by-reference are gone; --min-read-length defaults to 50. Fasta reads skip fastp and are filtered by length. Templated assembly aligns pairs with minimap2 -ax sr and calls samtools consensus -X hiseq (call quality at least 20, as BACoN's unreleased change at the time of the fork). De novo assembly: SKESA ( -a skesa ; the recommended de novo assembler — on the real-data benchmark its SNP distances matched SPAdes' with far fewer contigs) or SPAdes ( -a spades , --isolate ; writes the assembly graph, more robust below ~30x depth). Flye and myloasm are gone, with --read-type and --min-size . --snp-method auto is minimap2 for templated assemblies and SKA2 for SPAdes and SKESA assemblies. -m/--memory also sizes SPAdes and SKESA (it was BBDuk-only). A paired sample X next to a sample named X_R1 or X_R2 is an error (their outputs would collide). No assembler flags circular contigs any more, so SKA2's circular-contig end extension no longer applies. Single-end extraction matches read names with a trailing /1 or /2 stripped, as aligners report them. Output folders of BACoN do not resume under RASHER (the checkpoint fingerprints are seeded with the tool's name; every step runs again); BACoN VCFs are rewritten. Checkpoints record each step's own output signature, and a result is only reused when its output is still the file it wrote: a sample returning to a sheet can no longer pick up reads another sample wrote over. Switching a sample between single-end and paired (or fasta and fastq) removes the other shape's files. BBDuk's paired outputs are checked mate against mate, like minimap2's (a desynchronised pair fails the sample); mates named .1 / .2 ( fastq-dump --readids ) pair; the unpaired-reads file of fasterq-dump --split-3 next to its pair is skipped with a warning; a file cannot pair with a link to itself, and files that look like mates but do not pair are warned about. Stale fastp reports are removed on rerun and for samples that fail at baiting. The report and MultiQC drop the circular-contigs column (no short-read assembler flags circles) and say that read pairs were kept whole when either mate matched.

summary: Entity Matching identifies records that refer to the same real-world entity across one or more data sources. It is a key step in data integration and data cleaning. In practice, real-world datasets are often incomplete, and missing attribute values can significantly reduce the accuracy of traditional and learning-based methods. This presentation introduces a technique that uses Sentence Transformers to address EM under incomplete data. Records are represented as dense semantic embeddings, which allows the approach to capture contextual similarity between tuples even when some attribute values are missing. These embeddings support both the recovery of missing information and the matching of records. Experiments on benchmark datasets with varying levels of missingness show that the approach improves the robustness of entity matching on incomplete data.
title: A Sentence Transformer Based Technique for Entity Matching within Incomplete Data

summary: This record contains the scenario bank, raw transcripts and supporting files for the study " A Faith-Aware Ethical Violation Taxonomy for LLMs in Mental Health Counseling with an Islamic Case Study " (submitted to JMIR Mental Health). Mainly, 2 LLMs, Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5, were each run through 25 scripted multi-turn scenarios (92 user turns) in which a Muslim user presents religious or mental health concerns. Both models were accessed through OpenRouter with the same system prompt and default parameters. Contents - Scenario_Bank_25_Scenarios.pdf and scenario_turns.json: the final scripted scenarios, as a document and in machine-readable form. - ETHICS_CHECK_CLAUDE.ipynb and ETHICS_CHECK_GPT.ipynb: the raw interactive transcripts, deposited as run. - README_user_turn_provenance.md: for each scenario and model, the source file and how the entered user turns compare with the script. - User_Turn_Deviations.pdf: itemised differences between the scripted and the entered user turns. - run_scripted.py: a replication script that sends the scripted turns directly. It was not used to generate the reported data. - OpenRouter_Activity_Deposit.xlsx: the request-level log of the model calls. - Multimedia_Appendix_1 to _4: copies of the paper's appendices (each also has its own DOI). - Stage1_Draft_Scenarios_Gemini_Archive.pdf: archive of the earlier stage-1 draft scenarios (provisional codes); superseded by the final scenario bank. Notes on provenance - User turns were scripted in advance but entered manually, one at a time, in the same order for both models. Claude Opus 4.8's entered turns matched the script in 24 scenarios; in A1, T2 was entered twice. GPT-5.5's entered turns matched the script or differed only in punctuation or a stray quotation mark in 15 scenarios; in C4 it received one extra turn; in 7 scenarios the wording differed (about 5% of all scripted words); and the first three turns of C2 and C3 were not echoed in the notebook output (entered from the scenario document). Details are in User_Turn_Deviations.pdf. The coding evidence is provided in Multimedia Appendix 3 of the paper.
title: A Faith-Aware Ethical Violation Taxonomy for LLMs in Mental Health Counseling with an Islamic Case Study

summary: Adds the gap-filled sea-surface-temperature field as HEALPix NetCDF ( results/sst_gap_filled_healpix.nc , nside 32, NESTED): observed Copernicus Marine L3S, L4 reference, harmonic and scattering-transform (FOSCAT) fills, cloud and ocean masks, for 2026-04-01. A re-run on 2026-10-24 reproduces the published result within 0.4 %: FOSCAT RMSE 0.985 K (published 0.989 K), harmonic baseline 11.463 K (identical), 91.4 % improvement either way. The FOSCAT optimisation is not bit-reproducible.
